title: 20 Weekend Plans for Every Mood, and the Small Things That Help Them Happen
dek: Twenty things to do this weekend, sorted by mood, each with the small thing that makes it easier, plus a simple three-part plan so Saturday doesn't dissolve into errands and the sofa.

body.text: By Sunday at seven, plenty of weekends are a blur of laundry, a brunch that ate the afternoon and a great deal of lying down. Resting isn't wasting. The real culprit is drift: nothing planned, so nothing happens, and then you feel faintly robbed.
A little shape fixes most of it. Here's one method, then twenty ideas sorted by mood to hang on it.
One anchor, one treat, one rest

items: **One anchor.** The single thing the day is about. Not a list. A hike, a market, a class, a dinner.
**One treat.** A small nice thing attached to it: the good coffee, a longer bath, a new notebook.
**One rest.** A protected stretch of doing nothing useful, with no apology.

body.text: Do that for each day and you get two small plans, much less guilt, and space for chores around the edges. An anchor should take no more than half a day. If you catch yourself stacking three into one day, keep the one you're most curious about and move the rest to next weekend.
If you want to make something

body.title: Shape a ring dish from clay
body.note: Air-dry clay, a rolling pin or a bottle, and an afternoon. Paint it once it has dried. [Here's the beginner guide](/journal/how-to-start-air-dry-clay). **What makes it easier:** air-dry clay, a small set of sculpting tools and a craft mat, so the table stays clean and the edges come out crisp.

body.title: Start a junk journal
body.note: Gather the week's paper scraps and build a spread. [Here's how](/journal/how-to-start-junk-journaling). **What makes it easier:** {{product:stationery-island-a5-blank-journal-180-pages|a thick-paged notebook}}, a glue stick and a few rolls of {{product:mr-pen-washi-tape-21-rolls|washi tape}}, so the week's scraps become a spread.

body.title: Bake the ambitious thing
body.note: The recipe you've been avoiding: cinnamon rolls, a layer cake, a proper loaf. Weekends exist for projects with rising time.
body.first: Read the whole recipe on Friday and check you have the ingredients and the time.

body.title: For a make-something Saturday
body.dek: A block of clay, a small set of tools, a thick-paged journal and washi tape: kept in one drawer, they turn an open afternoon into a finished thing.

body.text: If you want to get outside

body.title: Take a short hike
body.note: Pick an easy, well-marked trail, check the weather, carry water and tell someone where you're headed. Going with a friend is the safer choice when you can. **Worth bringing:** walking shoes with some grip, trekking-style socks, a small daypack and a water bottle, so water and a snack ride on your back; a phone armband keeps a map or music in reach.

body.title: Have a proper picnic
body.note: A blanket, something good to eat, somewhere green. The [picnic guide](/journal/how-to-plan-a-perfect-picnic) has the whole checklist. **What makes it easier:** a picnic blanket and an insulated flask, so you have somewhere comfortable to sit and something warm to drink.

body.title: Watch the sunset on purpose
body.note: Check the local sunset time, bring a layer and find an open spot. An hour, and it feels like a mini holiday. **Worth bringing:** a picnic blanket and an insulated flask, so the hour outside stays comfortable as the air cools.

body.title: Browse a farmers' or flea market
body.note: Go early with a tote and a small budget. Come home with one thing you really like. **Worth bringing:** a roomy market tote, so the one thing you really like gets home in one piece.
body.first: Decide on a small budget and one thing to look for before you leave the house.

body.title: Walk somewhere you've never been
body.note: Choose a neighborhood, park or path you haven't explored and wander without a destination. Pack a snack. **Worth bringing:** comfortable walking shoes and a phone armband, so you can set off without a destination and keep your music or map in reach.

body.title: Be a tourist in your own town
body.note: Walk the main street as if you were visiting. Look up. Read the signs you've passed a hundred times. **Worth bringing:** a pocket notebook, so the signs you've passed a hundred times get written down.

body.title: For the park and the trail
body.dek: Walking shoes, a small daypack, a bottle, a blanket, a flask and a phone armband: the bag that makes leaving the house the easy option.

body.title: Host a craft night
body.note: Snacks, supplies, everyone makes something, even a first [crochet](/journal/how-to-start-crocheting) square, an [embroidery](/journal/how-to-start-embroidery) hoop or a little [watercolor](/journal/watercolor-painting-for-beginners) painting. A craft night is among the lowest-effort ways to see friends properly. [Here's how to host one](/journal/how-to-host-a-craft-night). **What makes it easier:** a friendship bracelet kit or a beginner kit for each guest, so nobody arrives to an empty table.

body.title: Hold a board-game afternoon
body.note: Bring out a game and a pot of something warm. Old-fashioned, and reliably better than expected. **What makes it easier:** a board game or two and a small tea set, so the table is ready before anyone arrives.

body.title: For an afternoon with friends
body.dek: A board game, a bracelet kit or a group painting kit gives everyone something to do with their hands while you catch up.

items: On Thursday or Friday evening, choose one anchor for each weekend day.
Attach a treat to each: a coffee, a snack, a playlist.
Put them in your calendar as appointments, with times, and book anything that needs booking.
Message anyone involved while you still have the energy.

body.text: When the plan falls apart anyway

It rains, a friend cancels, you wake up flat. Keep a short backup list: one outdoor option, one at-home option, one that takes under thirty minutes. Then you're choosing from a menu rather than starting from scratch, and a cancelled plan turns into a different plan instead of a lost day. [More weekend adventures](/journal/cheap-weekend-adventures) and [affordable hobbies](/journal/affordable-hobbies-under-25) have more ideas to keep on that list.

Want the shape without the thinking? Plan my weekend: Make Some Plans will build one around your mood, time and budget. For a fuller, four-part day, see [how to plan a solo Saturday](/journal/how-to-plan-a-solo-saturday).
Nine more ways to fill a weekend that need nothing but the time.

body.title: Run a book swap
body.note: Everyone brings two finished books and goes home with two new ones. **Worth bringing:** a canvas tote each, so the two new books get home safely.

body.title: Invite someone on a walk and coffee
body.note: Easier to say yes to than dinner, and just as good for catching up. **Worth bringing:** a thermos flask, if you'd rather take the coffee to the park.

body.title: Cook a big batch together
body.note: Make one large pot of something with a friend, then split it into containers for the week.

body.title: Cook something slow and fancy
body.note: A recipe with several steps, music on, and the cooking as the evening's activity rather than the chore before it.

body.title: Visit a museum or gallery
body.note: Some have free days or reduced entry, so check locally. Choose one room and stay an hour. **Worth bringing:** a pocket notebook for the details you want to keep.

body.title: Poke around a secondhand shop, bookstore or library
body.note: Set one rule: buy or borrow only what you can picture in your home.

body.title: Watch a film in broad daylight
body.note: Afternoon viewing feels delightfully illicit. Draw the curtains and make it an event. **Nice to have:** a soft throw and flameless candles, so the curtains-drawn afternoon feels like an event.

body.title: Nap without an alarm
body.note: A short one, ideally 20 to 30 minutes, guilt-free, with your phone in another room.

body.title: Plan next week on paper
body.note: Fifteen minutes with a planner and a pen makes Monday kinder. Put one plan in it that's just for you. **What makes it easier:** a pocket notebook or planner, so Monday's one fun plan is somewhere you will see it.
